_comment: Two light sources that do not match -- grey daylight and one warm bulb -- is what makes a domestic interior read as a real room rather than a set. It is also the hardest thing here for a model to hold, so this is a good preset to check adherence against.
label: The kitchen table

prompt._comment: Brown wall tiles and patterned lino do more period work than any single object in the frame. Keep them.
prompt.scene: a small kitchen with brown wall tiles half way up the wall, patterned lino underfoot, a wooden table pushed against the wall, net curtains gone yellow at the window, a filter coffee machine and a radio on the counter
prompt.light: grey early light through the net curtains and one warm bulb over the table still switched on, the two colours plainly not matching
prompt.lens: wide in a small space, the near edge of the table close to the camera and the counter behind going soft
prompt.framing: seated at the table, chest-up, turned towards the window
prompt._moment: What is HAPPENING, not what is in frame. A brief with no action in it is a portrait brief, and the model answers it with a portrait -- squared to the camera, arms hanging, waiting. Somebody caught halfway through something ordinary is what a real snapshot looks like.
prompt.moment: a cup halfway up and stopped there, mid-sentence
prompt.eraProps: a filter coffee machine with a glass jug, a wired telephone on the wall, a tin of loose tea, a folded newspaper, a wall clock with hands

motionHint: steam lifts off the cup, the net curtain breathes at the window, and the second hand moves on the clock
_scripts: Three fifteen-second scripts, one picked per order by the scripted arc (compose/prompt.mjs). Each is three shots at five seconds, written around the objects already in this place, so what happens comes from where it is. Every shot names the person, the first has them turned toward the lens, the last keeps their whole head in frame and ends on them, and none names anybody holding the camera. Tests in compose-prompt.test.js hold every one of those.

scripts.name: The coffee
shots: Medium. They are pouring coffee from the glass jug of the filter machine, turned toward the lens, camera holding on them.
Medium. They sit down at the wooden table with the cup and blow on it, steam lifting off it, camera easing round to stay in front of them.
Medium close. They raise the cup to the lens as if in a toast, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

scripts.name: The radio
shots: Medium. They are turning the dial on the radio on the counter, turned toward the lens, camera holding on them.
Wide. A song catches and they dance a few steps across the patterned lino, the net curtain breathing at the window, camera moving with them.
Medium close. They point at the lens and laugh, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

scripts.name: The telephone
shots: Medium. They are at the wooden table with a folded newspaper as the wired telephone on the wall starts to ring, turned toward the lens, camera holding on them.
Medium. They pick up the receiver and talk, laughing, the second hand moving on the clock, camera easing round to stay in front of them.
Medium close. They cover the receiver and mouth something to the lens, their whole head in frame, camera settling on them.

lookOverride._comment: A dim interior on a consumer CCD meant gain, and gain meant grain -- this is the reason the override mechanism exists at all. Amber up for the tungsten bulb, saturation down because gain washes colour out, halation open for the bulb itself.

ambience._comment: A fridge and a small room. Almost nothing: breakfast at a kitchen table is the quietest place in the catalog and should sound like it.

tone._comment: The wall clock this preset's own eraProps names, and whose second hand the motionHint already says moves. A tick is not noise and not a hum -- it is a single brief click once a second, which is exactly what tickHz buys that the ambience block above cannot: mod(t,1) gates a 2400 Hz partial on for 20ms out of every 1000ms and silent the rest, so the INTEGRATED loudness contribution stays tiny (2% duty cycle) even though the instantaneous burst is louder than a continuous tone would need to be to read as a click at all. 2400 Hz sits well inside the mic's 8 kHz ceiling and above the room tone's own 500 Hz lowpass, so it is never confused with the fridge hum underneath it.
